question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to create or reuse globally shared MCP declarations, and which host authorization or broker controls are required before that is safe?
rationale: The code can add executable and remote MCP capabilities to shared configuration, but choosing whether Claws may own that authority is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP ownership
options.body: Allow the feature only after commands, remote endpoints, and shared reuse pass an explicit host authorization boundary.

options.title: Permit referenced declarations only
options.body: Keep Claws read-only for preconfigured MCP resources and do not let manifests create or claim global declarations.

options.title: Pause the MCP slice pending the RFC
options.body: Keep the stacked branch open until the RFC establishes the canonical lifecycle owner and threat model.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP ownership
recommendation.body: Allow the feature only after commands, remote endpoints, and shared reuse pass an explicit host authorization boundary.
